clue.text: Author, one making correction, by sound of it

indicators.note: 'by sound of it' says the letters come from what the phrase sounds like, not how it is spelt

parts.note: someone who puts things right is a righter

explanation.surface: An author, perhaps an editor at heart, seems to be busy fixing things.
explanation.walkthrough: RIGHTER is rarely used as a word, but it is fair: one who rights, that is corrects, a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an author is someone who writes books, a writer by profession.

clue.text: One painted a god, icon, in new way

indicators.note: putting the letters 'in a new way' means rearranging them

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a deity as an icon in a novel style.
explanation.walkthrough: La Gioconda is the Italian name for the Mona Lisa, the lady Leonardo painted; 'One painted' means one who was painted, not a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gioconda is the sitter in the Mona Lisa, the most famous one painted.

clue.text: Avoid clipped military command

definitions.meaning: to keep away from someone deliberately

explanation.walkthrough: The drill-sergeant's 'Attention!' is barked as ''SHUN!', a clipped form of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun is to avoid; ''shun' is the shortened parade-ground order for attention.

clue.text: Period, yet to finish, in aroused post-war amusement — dry it's not!

indicators.note: the shortened period sits in the mixed letters
'aroused' stirs POSTWAR up, so its letters are mixed
a word yet to finish has not reached its last letter, so that letter goes

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A spell of excitement from post-war entertainment, with a nudge that it is anything but dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole tail: an amusement that is not dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A water sport, such as sailing or swimming, is a pastime you get wet at.

clue.text: Antagonise using a story in canteen regularly

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: 'regularly' keeps every other letter of 'in canteen'

explanation.surface: Someone upsets people by telling a tale in the staff canteen time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a position word putting LIE inside something, but it is part of the fodder for the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to antagonise them, turning them against you.

clue.text: On returning, well off, embracing wife in city

indicators.note: a word returning comes back the way it went, so ON reads NO

explanation.surface: A wealthy man comes home to the city with his wife on his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The W goes after the R of RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, in eastern England.

clue.text: Beginners go down these

parts.note: reads as novices at anything; here they are learner skiers
sounds like descending stairs or failing, but means skiing downhill

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down' suggests failing or descending a staircase; here it is skiing downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery slopes are the gentle ski runs where learners start.

clue.text: Wind, fair, beginning to end, near ground

indicators.note: the first letter of FAIR is sent to the end

parts.note: something low is near the ground

explanation.surface: A forecast: fair winds all day, blowing close to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIR sends its F to the back, becoming AIRF. 'Fair' reads as a weather word but is only fodder to be rotated.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind is simply moving air, so a current or airflow is a plain synonym for it.

clue.text: Money study, ultimately dreary

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: 'ultimately' points to the last letter of dreary

explanation.surface: The study of money, economics, turns out to be dull in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'the ready' is cash to hand, ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready, or readies, is informal British English for money.

clue.text: Initially ignored some chow mein he prepared for my return?

indicators.note: fodder that is prepared has been worked into a new form
the initial letter of 'some' is ignored

explanation.surface: A takeaway ready for someone coming back: some chow mein he cooked for my return.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a scene of its own; the definition is the question at the end, asking when the meal is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for my return is done for when I come home.

clue.text: Reserve surprisingly nice tree, cheap initially

indicators.note: the letters turn up in a surprising order
'initially' takes the first letter of cheap

explanation.surface: Someone books a pleasant tree for a bargain price, to their surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a verb about booking; it is the noun meaning restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is reserve, a reluctance to speak freely.

clue.text: Some serenade leading singer

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'serenade leading' are wanted

explanation.surface: Part of a serenade goes to the lead vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Adele is the London-born pop star behind albums such as 21 and 25.

clue.text: At work use one lorry in wrong way

indicators.note: letters at work are being moved about

explanation.surface: On the job, a driver takes a single truck the wrong way down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At work' reads as setting the scene at the workplace; it is what makes the letters move.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means mistaken or incorrect, so the adverb describes acting by mistake.

clue.text: Overbearing pop singers must reform

indicators.note: the letters must take a new form

explanation.surface: Arrogant pop stars need to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overbearing' looks like a description of the singers but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe crushing, domineering behaviour that weighs heavily on people.

clue.text: Son leaving girl to become fighter

indicators.note: SON leaves the name, so those letters go

explanation.surface: A boy walks out on his girlfriend and turns into a brawler.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is ALISON, which ends in SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight boxing champion.

clue.text: Chatter ox

definitions.meaning: idle, incessant talk, as a verb
the long-haired ox of the Himalayas

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is to chatter; a yak is a long-haired Himalayan ox.

clue.text: Hear thieves? Nonsense!

indicators.note: 'Hear' asks for the word as it is heard

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal, so thieves are nickers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knickers!' is a British exclamation of scornful disbelief; knickers are also women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying 'Knickers!' is saying 'Nonsense!'

clue.text: Potential killer when provoked at first

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: 'at first' takes the first letter of provoked

explanation.surface: Something that only turns deadly once it is provoked.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an &lit: a snake is a potential killer when provoked. 'at first' belongs only to provoked.
explanation.definitionFit: An asp is a venomous snake, famously Cleopatra's killer.

clue.text: Away from France

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
F is France's international vehicle code

explanation.walkthrough: 'Away from France' reads as abroad; the definition is only 'Away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Off means away, as in 'he's off today'.

clue.text: Convincing Catholic to cut minor weakness

parts.note: a foible is a minor weakness

explanation.surface: A persuasive Catholic curbs a small failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor weakness' is a two-word definition of the host, not 'minor' as a separate clue to something small.
explanation.definitionFit: A forcible case carries force and persuades strongly, the sense of 'convincing'.

clue.text: Morale for example comes to nothing

explanation.surface: Morale, say, amounts to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes to nothing' reads as a single idea, failure; it splits into a link and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego, a sense of self-worth, is close to morale.

clue.text: Garland's free time? Not sure

indicators.note: 'Not sure' means the word SURE is not there

explanation.surface: Judy Garland's time off? Nobody is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garland’s' tempts toward Judy Garland; it is a plain garland, with ’s standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Hawaiians hang a ring of flowers round a visitor's neck.

clue.text: Better grid after review involving new tests here

indicators.note: a grid after review has been reworked, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A crossword setter improves a grid after reviewing it, with new tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tests' reads as trials of the grid; they are Test matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Trent Bridge is the Nottingham cricket ground where Test matches are played.

clue.text: Mock pronunciation of river

indicators.note: the answer is how the river's name is pronounced

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Someone makes fun of how a river's name is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock pronunciation' suggests a fake accent; 'Mock' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean making fun of someone, poking gentle ridicule.

clue.text: Radio presenter's shortened act getting the bird

indicators.note: the act is shortened by losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A DJ's cut-short act is booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' is British for being jeered; here it just adds JAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A deejay is a disc jockey, a radio presenter who plays records.

clue.text: Genuine Dad crossing this country park finally

parts.note: for a British setter, this country is the UK

indicators.note: 'finally' takes the last letter of park

explanation.surface: A real father walking across a national park at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Pukka, from Hindi, is British slang for genuine or first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pukka is genuine, the real thing.

clue.text: Ignite dispute about female anger

indicators.note: about means the dispute goes around the other pieces, wrapping them

explanation.surface: A row over a woman's fury is about to flare.
explanation.walkthrough: A set-to is British for a brief heated quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignite means start burning, and the phrase is the everyday way of saying so.

clue.text: Change of heart in Helen's place for politician

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letters, is changed round

explanation.surface: A politician has a change of heart in Helen's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of TROY is RO; changing it gives OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a member of Britain's Conservative Party, in Parliament or standing for it.

clue.text: Scottish politician sets aside time for theatre worker

parts.note: Nicola Sturgeon, former First Minister of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish politician takes time off to work in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' means the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals call the room where operations happen a theatre, and the surgeon performs there.

clue.text: Demob contract soldiers found earlier

indicators.note: the soldiers are found earlier in the answer than the contract

explanation.surface: Soldiers find their discharge came earlier than their contract said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found earlier' puts the soldiers before the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob, short for demobilise, means discharging troops from the armed forces after a war.
